# react-native-liquid-glassmorphism

> Liquid Glass for React Native, on **both iOS and Android**, from one declarative component. Glass views **merge into one liquid body when they come close, on both platforms** — the only React Native library that does this on Android. iOS 26 renders Apple's native `UIGlassEffect`; Android reproduces the same optics in a real-time AGSL refractive-lens shader (per-frame backdrop capture → blur → rounded-glass lozenge with edge refraction, chromatic dispersion, mirrored edge reflection, Fresnel rim, and tilt/touch specular). Also searched for as: React Native liquid glass, glassmorphism, frosted glass, glass effect, iOS 26 glass, backdrop blur, blur view, AGSL glass, Android liquid glass.

Package: `react-native-liquid-glassmorphism` (npm, MIT).
Component: `<LiquidGlassView>`.
Requires React Native 0.83+. Fabric (New Architecture) and the old architecture both supported. **Not usable in Expo Go** — it is a native module, so use a development build or `expo prebuild`.

- Docs: https://himanshu-lal4.github.io/react-native-liquid-glassmorphism
- Repo: https://github.com/himanshu-lal4/react-native-liquid-glassmorphism
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-native-liquid-glassmorphism

## Install

```sh
npm install react-native-liquid-glassmorphism
# or: yarn add react-native-liquid-glassmorphism
# Expo (development build / prebuild — NOT Expo Go):
npx expo install react-native-liquid-glassmorphism
```

Then rebuild the native app (`pod install` + run for iOS, a fresh Gradle build for Android). There is no JS-only path: React Native has no `backdrop-filter`, so backdrop treatment requires a native view.

## Minimal example

```tsx
import { LiquidGlassView } from 'react-native-liquid-glassmorphism';

<LiquidGlassView
  variant="regular"
  tintColor="rgba(10,132,255,0.5)"
  borderRadius={24}
  interactive
  style={{ padding: 20 }}
>
  <Text>Content renders crisply on top of the glass</Text>
</LiquidGlassView>
```

Children render sharp on top; only the backdrop *behind* the view is blurred, tinted and refracted.

## Props

All optional. `LiquidGlassViewProps` extends `ViewProps`.

**Material**

- `preset`: `'navigationBar' | 'floatingTabBar' | 'cardOverMedia' | 'compactControl' | 'frosted' | 'crystal'`. A tuned starting point, resolved as `{ ...preset, ...yourProps }` — any prop you pass explicitly wins.
- `accessibilityMode`: `'auto' | 'forceGlass' | 'forceOpaque'` (default `'auto'`). **Both platforms.** `auto` renders an opaque surface instead of glass when the platform asks for reduced transparency (iOS Reduce Transparency; Android high-contrast text, the closest available signal), and drops `tilt` under Reduce Motion. `forceGlass` overrides the transparency preference but still honours Reduce Motion. `forceOpaque` always renders opaque. Read live — change events plus a re-read when the app returns to the foreground, so no imperative refresh is needed. `interactive` is deliberately not suppressed, since it answers a touch the user just made.
- `variant`: `'regular' | 'clear'` (default `'regular'`). `regular` = adaptive frosted glass that lightens dark backdrops to keep text legible; `clear` = lighter, largely transparent refractive glass for use over photos and video.
- `tintColor`: `ColorValue`. Tint layered over the blurred backdrop. Use `rgba()` or 8-digit hex to control strength.
- `intensity`: number `0`–`100` (default `60`). Blur / material strength. On iOS 26 the OS manages the material, so this only drives the pre-26 `UIBlurEffect` fallback; on Android it scales the RenderEffect blur radius.
- `blurRadius`: number, dp. An explicit blur radius that overrides whatever `intensity` would derive. Useful range roughly `0`–`30`; `0` is genuinely unblurred. Honoured on **both** platforms including real Liquid Glass (on iOS the backdrop is blurred underneath the glass, which then refracts the blurred result). Reach for this instead of `intensity` on `clear` glass, which spans a much narrower range across the 0–100 scale.
- `dim`: number `0`–`1` (default `0`). A flat dimming scrim over the backdrop, drawn under the children. **Both platforms.** This is the modal-overlay primitive — a full-screen `<LiquidGlassView dim={0.4} blurRadius={24} rim={false} />` behind a sheet gives the blurred, darkened backdrop that pattern wants.

**Edges and light**

- `rim`: boolean (default `true`). Draw the bright glass edge.
- `specular`: boolean (default `true`). Draw the moving sheen and specular hotspot.
- `edgeReflectionStrength`: number `0`–`1` (default `1`). **Android only.** Strength of the mirrored "echo" band at the top/bottom rim. Independent of `thickness`, so you can keep a deep lens while calming the reflection over text-heavy backdrops. No-op on iOS.

**Geometry**

- `borderRadius`: number, dp (default `0`). Ignored when `shape` is set.
- `shape`: `LiquidGlassShape`. A custom silhouette — the glass *lenses the backdrop through the shape*, it does not merely clip a rectangle. Stretched to fill the view's bounds, so size the view to the shape's aspect ratio. iOS masks the glass with a `CAShapeLayer`; Android rasterises the path into a signed-distance-field texture the AGSL shader samples (API 33+; below that it degrades to a path-clipped frost).
- `thickness`: number `0`–`2` (default `1`). "Liquid volume" — scales refraction and lensing depth. `0` = flat pane, `1` = default, `~2` = deep lens. Intermediate values are Android only (iOS fixes the `UIGlassEffect` optics), but `0` is honoured on both.
- `secondaryShape`: `LiquidGlassShape`. **Android only.** A second glass body, smooth-min merged with `shape` on the distance field so the two cling and fuse as they approach — the mercury effect. Both shapes share the primary's view-box, so author them as `path`/`points` shapes positioned within one box; two bounds-filling primitives merge concentrically. The neck between the bodies is real glass with correct lensing, not two overlapping silhouettes. Works on BOTH platforms: Android merges the signed distance fields natively (cheaper, higher quality); iOS has no field to blend, so the merged outline is computed in JS and passed as one ordinary path. SET IT ONCE — DO NOT ANIMATE IT: changing either shape rebuilds the distance field on the CPU (~361ms for a 340x190dp body on a mid-range device), and animating the merge drove a test screen to 1.6fps.
- `shapeSmoothing`: number, dp (default `0`). **Both platforms.** Blend radius for the `secondaryShape` merge. `0` is a hard union with a visible crease. The bridge forms when the two surfaces are each within roughly `k/4` of the midpoint (`smin(d, d, k) = d - k/4`), so to fuse bodies `g` apart use a smoothing above about `2 * g`. `16`–`48` reads well for bodies ~100dp across.
- `refraction`: boolean (default `true`). **Android only, API 33+.** Dials the edge-refraction lens up (~1.35×). Lensing is intrinsic to the material and never fully off — use `thickness={0}` for a genuinely flat pane. No-op on iOS.

**Interaction**

- `interactive`: boolean (default `false`). iOS 26 interactive `UIGlassEffect`; on Android a touch-following specular highlight and optical magnification under the finger.
- `tilt`: boolean (default `false`). **Android only.** Device-tilt specular from the gyro/accelerometer. Deliberately separate from `interactive` so you can have touch response without an always-on motion sensor — leaving it off saves battery on persistent chrome. No-op on iOS.

**Legibility and performance**

- `legibilityFloor`: number `0`–`1` (default `0`). **Android only.** An adaptive veil drawn *under the foreground children only*, so icons and labels stay readable over `clear` glass without darkening the whole pane. Adapts to backdrop brightness and is hued by `tintColor`. No-op on iOS.
- `iridescence`: number `0`–`1` (default `0`). **Android only.** Rainbow shimmer at the rim, hue driven by the angle to the centre, riding the same edge ramp as the lens so it reads as light splitting at the edge rather than a colour overlay.
- `grain`: number `0`–`~0.15` (default `0`). **Android only.** Film grain. A heavy blur flattens the backdrop into a gradient; a little noise makes it read as etched glass. Above ~0.15 it reads as noise.
- `lightAngle`: number, radians (default `0`). **Android only.** Rotates the built-in light direction. An offset rather than an absolute bearing, so `0` keeps the tuned top-left key light. Drives the sheen band, specular hotspot and inner shadow together.
- `specularSharpness`: number (default `1`). **Android only.** Multiplier on the specular exponent; higher is a tighter, harder hotspot. Useful range `0.25`–`4`.
- `saturation`: number (default `1`). **Android only.** Multiplier on backdrop vibrancy, applied before the tint. `0` is greyscale. Useful range `0`–`2`.
- `brightness`: number (default `1`). **Android only.** Multiplier on backdrop luminance, before the tint. Unlike `dim` (a flat scrim on top) this grades what the glass transmits, so the edge and sheen keep their own brightness. Useful range `0.5`–`1.5`.
- `magnification`: number (default `1`). **Android only.** Constant magnification of the backdrop through the lens centre; above 1 the glass reads as convex. Distinct from the transient touch magnifier `interactive` adds. Useful range `0.5`–`2`.
- `ior`: number (default `1.5`). **Android only.** Index of refraction. `1.5` is window glass and reproduces the default look, `1` is no bending at all, `2.4` is roughly diamond. Related to `thickness` but distinct — `thickness` is how deep the glass is, `ior` is what it is made of. Useful range `1`–`2.5`.
- `frameStatsInterval`: number, ms (default `0`). **Android only.** How often `onFrameStats` reports. `0` disables timing entirely — it is a permission, not just a cadence. A development HUD; ship it off.
- `paused`: boolean (default `false`). **Android only.** Suspend the effect without unmounting; the glass holds its last frame and re-captures on resume. Views Android already reports as off-screen pause automatically — use this for cases that signal cannot see, such as a screen kept alive in a navigator stack or an off-screen carousel page. No-op on iOS.

**Events**

- `onPipelineReady`: `(e: NativeSyntheticEvent<GlassPipelineInfo>) => void`. Fires once per view after the first frame, reporting the tier that *actually* rendered: `{ tier, osVersion, shaderCompiled, supportsNativeGlass }`. Fires on every platform, including the web fallback with `tier: 'none'`.
- `onError`: `(e: NativeSyntheticEvent<GlassErrorInfo>) => void`. Fires when the view cannot do what the props asked: `{ code, message, fatal }`. Each code fires at most once per view and most are non-fatal — the view recovered but is not rendering exactly what you asked for.
- `onFrameStats`: `(e: NativeSyntheticEvent<GlassFrameStats>) => void`. **Android only.** Frame timings aggregated over each `frameStatsInterval` window: `{ drawFps, totalMs, maxTotalMs, captureMs, shaderMs, tier, capturedWidth, capturedHeight }`. Frames in a window are averaged, not sampled, and the worst is carried as `maxTotalMs` — read that when hunting jank. CPU-side only; GPU shader execution is not visible.

## LiquidGlassContainer

Cross-view merging: glass children fuse into one liquid body as they come close, instead of stacking as separate panes. This is the library's headline differentiator — it works on BOTH platforms, and no other React Native library does it on Android.

Import: `import { LiquidGlassContainer } from 'react-native-liquid-glassmorphism'`

- `spacing`: number, dp (default `0`). The distance at which children begin to merge. `0` disables merging and children render as ordinary separate glass.

Any `<LiquidGlassView>` merges just by being a descendant — there is no per-child prop and no special child component. Merging is a relationship between siblings, so the container defines the group and the distance.

Children can be moved by position, `transform` or layout animation: the container reads each child's real on-screen geometry every frame, so an animated merge costs a uniform upload rather than a rebuild. That is the difference from `secondaryShape`, which bakes a distance field and is static only.

iOS uses `UIGlassContainerEffect` (iOS 26+); the OS performs the merge. Below iOS 26 children render as ordinary separate glass. Android has no OS equivalent, so the container renders one glass surface and smooth-mins the children's rounded rectangles per pixel in AGSL. Android limits: bodies are rounded rectangles from each child's size and `borderRadius` (a child with a custom `shape` is not merged), and at most 8 children merge because the shader's uniform array needs a compile-time bound — beyond that they render as ordinary glass and the dev build warns once. The merged surface adopts the material of the first body it merges.

```tsx
<LiquidGlassContainer spacing={40}>
  <LiquidGlassView style={{ width: 96, height: 96, borderRadius: 48 }} />
  <LiquidGlassView style={{ width: 96, height: 96, borderRadius: 48 }} />
</LiquidGlassContainer>
```

## ScrollEdgeBlurView

A second component for progressive edge blur — content scrolling under a header or tab bar. Takes no children, no silhouette, no tint, no interaction, and never intercepts touches.

Import: `import { ScrollEdgeBlurView } from 'react-native-liquid-glassmorphism'`

- `edge`: `'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right'` (default `'top'`). The edge the blur is anchored to; it dissolves toward the opposite side.
- `maxBlurRadius`: number, dp (default `24`). Blur radius at the anchored edge. Deliberately dp rather than raw pixels. On iOS this picks the nearest discrete `UIBlurEffect` material, since UIKit exposes no continuous radius.
- `falloff`: number `0`–`1` (default `1`). How far across the view the blur has fully dissolved.

Android: reads the same shared per-root backdrop capture the glass views use, so it costs no extra capture on a screen that already has glass; needs API 31+, renders nothing below. The ramp is an opacity ramp over one blurred layer, not a per-pixel radius ramp. iOS: a `UIVisualEffectView` masked by a `CAGradientLayer`. Web: an inert transparent view that holds its layout.

```tsx
<ScrollEdgeBlurView
  edge="top"
  maxBlurRadius={32}
  falloff={0.8}
  style={{ position: 'absolute', top: 0, left: 0, right: 0, height: 120 }}
/>
```

## Plain blur mode

To use this as a conventional backdrop blur — a drop-in for `BlurView` — turn off every glass signal:

```tsx
<LiquidGlassView rim={false} specular={false} thickness={0} blurRadius={20} />
```

On iOS that combination tells the library you do not want Liquid Glass at all, and it renders a plain `UIBlurEffect` material (picking the nearest discrete material to your radius) instead of `UIGlassEffect`.

## Shapes

```tsx
{ type: 'circle' }
{ type: 'squircle', n?: number }                 // n=2 ellipse, 4 classic squircle (default), higher is boxier
{ type: 'polygon', sides: number, rotation?: number, cornerRadius?: number }
{ type: 'star', points?: number, innerRatio?: number }   // defaults 5 and 0.5; smaller innerRatio is spikier
{ type: 'points', points: Array<[number, number]> }      // any coordinate space; bounding box becomes the view-box
{ type: 'path', d: string, width: number, height: number }
```

`path` supports `M/L/H/V/C/S/Q/T/Z`, absolute and relative. Elliptic arcs (`A`) are **not** supported — express curves as cubic or quadratic béziers. Concave shapes, such as a tab-bar notch, are fully supported.

## Presets

`GlassPresets` is a frozen map of partial prop bags; `GLASS_PRESET_NAMES` lists the keys.

| Preset | variant | intensity | thickness | edgeReflectionStrength | legibilityFloor | borderRadius | extra |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `navigationBar` | regular | 70 | 0.6 | 0.4 | 0.15 | 0 |
| `floatingTabBar` | regular | 65 | 1 | 1 | 0.2 | 28 |
| `cardOverMedia` | clear | 45 | 1.2 | 0.7 | 0.35 | 24 |
| `compactControl` | clear | 50 | 0.7 | 1 | 0.25 | 20 |
| `frosted` | regular | 85 | 0.4 | 0.3 | 0 | 20 | (+ `grain` 0.05) |
| `crystal` | clear | 30 | 1.8 | 1 | 0.1 | 24 | (+ `iridescence` 0.45) |

```tsx
<LiquidGlassView preset="floatingTabBar" borderRadius={32} />
```

## Capability detection

```tsx
import {
  getGlassCapabilities,   // () => GlassCapabilities — answers before anything renders
  isLiquidGlassSupported, // () => boolean
  useGlassSupport,        // () => GlassCapabilities — the hook form
} from 'react-native-liquid-glassmorphism';
```

`GlassCapabilities` is `{ tier, osVersion, supportsBlur, supportsRefraction, ... }`.

`GlassTier` is `'glass' | 'refraction' | 'blur' | 'tint' | 'none'`. Use `getGlassCapabilities()` to decide whether to mount a glass view at all; use `onPipelineReady` to learn what a mounted view actually did.

## Platform behaviour

| Platform | Tier | What renders |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iOS 26+ | `glass` | Apple's native `UIGlassEffect` — regular/clear, interactive, tint, corner radius, shape mask |
| iOS 15–25 | `blur` | `UIBlurEffect` material bucketed by `intensity` |
| Android 13+ (API 33+) | `refraction` | Per-frame backdrop capture → Gaussian blur → AGSL refractive-lens shader with SDF shapes |
| Android 12 (API 31–32) | `blur` | `RenderEffect` blur + tint |
| Android < 12 | `tint` | Translucent tint fallback |
| Web | `none` | Non-glass fallback; the library is mobile-focused |

## Error codes

`SHADER_COMPILE_FAILED` (AGSL would not compile, fell back a tier) · `PIPELINE_DEGRADED` (OS cannot run the requested tier) · `INVALID_SHAPE` (path unparseable, fell back to a rounded rectangle) · `BACKDROP_CAPTURE_FAILED` (a view behind the glass refused a software draw, reusing the previous backdrop) · `GLASS_UNAVAILABLE` (iOS below 26, `UIBlurEffect` standing in).

## How it compares

Honest positioning against the libraries it is usually weighed against:

- **`expo-blur`, `@react-native-community/blur`** — blur the backdrop but never bend it. Straight lines behind the panel stay straight. This library refracts: edge lensing, chromatic dispersion, mirrored edge reflection, Fresnel rim, interactive touch/tilt specular. They are lighter and have wider OS support; use them if a blur is all you need.
- **`expo-glass-effect`, `@callstack/liquid-glass`** — real Apple Liquid Glass, but **iOS only**. They are thinner wrappers over the OS material and excellent if you ship iOS-only. This library renders a matching glass effect on Android too.
- **`@uginy/react-native-liquid-glass`** — also does AGSL glass on Android. It renders its own glass on iOS rather than calling Apple's `UIGlassEffect`; this library uses the system material on iOS 26, so the iOS side is Apple's real glass rather than a reproduction of it. It also requires Android 13+, where this library falls back cleanly to API 24.
- **`react-native-android-liquid-glass`** — Android only, and a Fabric bridge over a third-party JitPack AAR rather than its own shader. That brings a JitPack repository declaration (which breaks under `FAIL_ON_PROJECT_REPOS`), an arm-only native binary (so blur kernels degrade on x86 emulators), a React Native 0.85+ floor, and no way to ship fixes that live upstream in the AAR.
- **`react-native-skia`** — maximum control if you want to write the effect yourself; this library is the batteries-included component.

Distinctive to this library:

- **Cross-view merging on both platforms.** `@callstack/liquid-glass` has a container too, but it is twenty lines around Apple's `UIGlassContainerEffect` and that package has no Android support at all. On Android the merge is done here with an analytic smooth-min in our own AGSL shader.

- Native `UIGlassEffect` on iOS 26 **and** an AGSL refraction shader on Android, from one API.
- **No third-party native dependency.** The AGSL is written in this repo — no JitPack repository to declare, no prebuilt AAR, no arm-only `.so`. It works on any ABI, including x86 emulators.
- **`minSdk` 24**, with a documented fallback ladder (refraction on API 33+, `RenderEffect` blur on 31–32, translucent tint below) rather than a hard Android 13 requirement.
- Signed-distance-field custom shapes including concave SVG silhouettes — no other option here has shape support beyond a corner radius.
- An Expo config plugin, runtime capability detection, and a web fallback.

## FAQ

**How do I add Liquid Glass to a React Native app?** Install the package, rebuild the native app, and wrap content in `<LiquidGlassView>`. No `backdrop-filter` exists in React Native, so a native view is required.

**Does it work on Android?** Yes. Android 13+ runs a real-time AGSL refraction shader that reproduces the iOS 26 optics. Android 12 gets blur + tint; below that, a translucent tint.

**Does it work in Expo?** Yes, with a development build or `expo prebuild`. **Not in Expo Go**, which cannot load custom native modules.

**Does it need iOS 26?** No. iOS 26 gets Apple's real `UIGlassEffect`; iOS 15–25 falls back to a `UIBlurEffect` material automatically.

**What is the difference between glassmorphism and Liquid Glass?** Glassmorphism is blur + translucency + tint — the backdrop is softened but its geometry is unchanged. Liquid Glass also *refracts*, bending and magnifying content at the rim. Straight lines behind a glassmorphic panel stay straight; behind Liquid Glass they curve near the edges.

**Can I use it as a plain blur view?** Yes — `rim={false} specular={false} thickness={0} blurRadius={20}`.

**Can the glass be a non-rectangular shape?** Yes — circle, squircle, polygon, star, explicit points, or an arbitrary concave SVG path. The backdrop is lensed through the silhouette, not clipped to it.

**Does it honour accessibility settings?** Yes, by default. `accessibilityMode="auto"` renders an opaque surface when the user has enabled Reduce Transparency (or high-contrast text on Android) and drops the tilt specular under Reduce Motion, updating live.

**Is it New Architecture compatible?** Yes — Fabric and the old architecture both work.

**Can glass views merge into each other?** Yes — wrap them in `<LiquidGlassContainer spacing={n}>` and any glass descendants fuse as they approach. Works on both platforms, and animating the children is cheap because the merge is analytic rather than a baked field.

**Is it free?** Yes, MIT licensed.
